title: Serve equivalent primary content on mobile and desktop
statement: The narrow-viewport rendering of a page contains the same primary content, headings, structured data, metadata, and internal links as the wide-viewport rendering, and does not omit sections or truncate text that only the wide layout shows.
rationale: Where indexing is performed from the mobile rendering, content present only in the wide layout is content the index never sees, so the desktop page can be complete while the indexed page is not.
implementation: Use one document that reflows rather than two documents selected by device, and where a section is collapsed on narrow screens keep its text in the markup instead of loading it on expand. If a separate mobile host exists, compare its content against the desktop host section by section.

verification.method: Render each significant route at a narrow and a wide viewport and diff the extracted text, headings, links, structured data, and metadata between them.

title: Fit primary content within the viewport width
statement: At a narrow viewport no primary content requires horizontal scrolling to read, and no fixed-width element, wide table, unconstrained image, or long unbroken string forces the document wider than the screen.
rationale: Horizontal scrolling to read a line of text makes reading a two-axis task, and the element that causes it is usually one component rather than the layout, so the whole page suffers for a single overflow.
implementation: Find the widest element at the narrow viewport and constrain that one rather than adding an overflow rule to the document. Wide tables can scroll within their own container, which keeps the surrounding text readable.

verification.method: Load each route at a narrow viewport and compare the document scroll width against the viewport width, reporting the widest contributing element.

title: Keep interstitials from obscuring the primary content
statement: A reader arriving from a link sees the content they came for without first dismissing a full-screen overlay, and any notice the site must show occupies a banner that leaves the content readable.
rationale: An overlay covering the content on arrival makes the page appear to be about the overlay, and the reader's first required action is unrelated to why they came.
implementation: Replace the full-screen overlay with an inline banner sized to leave the content visible, or defer the prompt until after the reader has engaged. Legally required notices can be shown in a banner rather than a blocking layer.

verification.method: Load each entry route at a narrow viewport as a first-time visitor and record the proportion of the viewport the content occupies before any interaction.

caution: The cited guidance names intrusive interstitials as a problem without publishing a measurable threshold, so the proportion at which a banner becomes an interstitial is a judgement this control records rather than computes.

title: Size interactive controls for touch input
statement: Controls a reader taps meet the published minimum target size, or are spaced far enough apart that the published exception applies.
rationale: A target smaller than the published minimum is missed often enough that the reader has to aim, and adjacent small targets convert a miss into the wrong action rather than no action.
implementation: Increase the control's padding rather than its font size, or increase the spacing between neighbours to satisfy the exception. Inline links within a paragraph are exempt under the criterion and need not be enlarged.

verification.method: Measure the rendered bounding box and neighbour spacing of every interactive control at a narrow viewport and report those below the published minimum without a qualifying exception.

title: Render body text at a readable size without zoom
statement: Body text is legible at the default zoom level on a narrow viewport, text scales when the reader increases it up to the published factor without content being lost, and the viewport declaration does not disable scaling.
rationale: Text small enough to require zooming means every reader pinches before reading, and a viewport declaration that forbids scaling removes their ability to do so at all.
implementation: Remove any maximum-scale or user-scalable restriction from the viewport declaration, set body text from a relative unit so it responds to the reader's preference, and check the layout still holds at the published scale factor.

verification.method: Inspect the viewport declaration for scaling restrictions and re-render each route at the published zoom factor, checking for clipped or overlapping content.
